legend: Diffuse effacement of the tonsillar architecture with expansion of the interfollicular regions by a heterogeneous lymphoplasmacytic population, with vague nodularity.
A Giemsa-stained imprint highlights interspersed immunoblastic cells, which are large and bear smooth chromatin and basophilic cytoplasm.

EBV-encoded small RNA (EBER) in situ hybridization: EBER positivity among cells of all sizes, including a few large immunoblasts scattered throughout. The heterogeneous EBER pattern is typical in polymorphic posttransplant lymphoproliferative disorder in children. When EBER positivity is present preferentially in larger cells or in sheets of cells, a diagnosis of polymorphic posttransplant lymphoproliferative disorder should be reconsidered.
The full morphological spectrum of B cells is seen, from round lymphocytes with mature, condensed chromatin to immunoblast-like and plasmacytic cells.

diagnosis: Monomorphic posttransplant lymphoproliferative disorder – plasma cell neoplasm
legend: This example is composed of mature plasma cells with uniform small round nuclei and the characteristic clockface chromatin pattern. A few intermingled small lymphocytes correspond to mature T cells. The range of B-cell maturity is absent (as expected in monomorphic patterns).

diagnosis: Monomorphic posttransplant lymphoproliferative disorder – plasma cell neoplasm
legend: CD138 staining shows a sheet-like plasma cell population expanding and distorting the underlying tonsillar architecture. EBV-encoded small RNA (EBER) (not shown) was negative in this case and is a feature somewhat enhanced in plasma cell posttransplant lymphoproliferative disorder.

diagnosis: Monomorphic posttransplant lymphoproliferative disorder – plasma cell neoplasm
legend: Plasma cells are kappa light chain–restricted.

legend:
15 year old male, 4 years post orthotopic heart transplant with adenotonsillar hypertrophy. Adenoid biposy sampled.

(L) H&E whole slide image showing expansion of adenoids with confluent, monotonous plasma cells. 

(C) CD138 immunohistochemistry highlights expansion of the plasma cell component.

(R) EBER in-situ hybridization is negative in this example of M-PLTD, plasmacytoma.

diagnosis: Monomorphic PTLD, Buriktt lymphoma, EBV positive
legend:
8 year old male, 3 years post orthotopic heart transplant with cervical adenopathy. Needle biopsy of enlarged lymph node performed. 

(L) H&E whole slide image showing monotonous population of medium-sized blastoid lymphocytes with areas of tumor necrosis. FISH studies confirm MYC rearrangement with IgL partner.

(C) Ki67 (MIB1) immunohistochemistry of corresponding needle biopsy with near 100% proliferation among viable tumor cells.

(R) EBER in-situ hybridization shows diffuse positivity among tumor cells.
